summary: Tested the new rule that free-trial users get one pronunciation analysis per trial word. Every requested check passed. (1) Trial user (logged in via /login, used a fake mic playing the cached 'party' clip): Record, Stop, Analyse returned practise-feedback with 100/100 Excellent. The button then changed to practise-join 'Join Pronounce This to keep practising', with the helper text 'Free trial includes one pronunciation check per word.' Clicking it opened paywall-modal; the subhead starts 'You've used your free pronunciation check for this word. Members get unlimited practice.' (2) Fresh session and reload, searched 'party' and recorded: the button was practise-join straight away, because status returned locked:true. Clicking it opened the same paywall, and no request was sent to /api/practice/assess (network capture showed only status + tts). Closing the paywall works. (3) Member: recorded and analysed 'party' twice. Both times practise-feedback appeared, the button stayed 'Analyse My Pronunciation' (practise-analyse), and no paywall appeared. Member has no practice_words in the DB. (4) Backend, using the legacy cookie: status for the trial user on 'party' gave locked:true; for 'PARTY ' (different case, trailing space) also locked:true; for 'hello' locked:false. Member gave locked:false. A trial POST to assess returned 402 {code:practice_exhausted, kind:practice} before any audio was processed. Azure calls used: 3. Cleanup done: practice_words removed for the trial user, and status now returns locked:false.

minor.issue: Race condition: _trial_used is checked before the Azure call and $addToSet runs only after it. A trial user who sends two assess requests at the same moment (e.g. a double click, or two tabs) can get 2 or more analyses for one word. The UI disables the button while busy, so this is low risk.

action_items: Optional: to close the race, reserve the trial slot atomically before calling Azure: update_one({email, practice_words:{$ne:norm}}, {$addToSet:...}). If matched_count is 0, return 402. If the result turns out unassessable, release the slot with $pull.
Optional UX: when locked is true the join CTA only appears after the user records a take. You could show it (or a note) before recording so trial users don't record for nothing.
critical_code_review_comments: practice.py: the lock is only set when out.assessable is true, so a failed or unclear take does not use up the trial. Good.
practice.py status: the word is normalised the same way as in assess (whitespace collapsed, lowercased). Checked: 'PARTY ' is locked.

PractiseWord.jsx: when locked is true, analyse() opens the paywall locally without calling the API. A 402 from the API sets locked and leaves the popup to the global interceptor, so the paywall is not opened twice.
The previous practise-feedback stays visible under the join CTA after the analysis that locks the word. That is good, since the user keeps their result.
